lesson.title: De matin à soir
lesson.subtitle: Chaining reflexives (se lever, se laver, s'habiller, se coucher) across a full day.

hook.title: From Morning Alarm to Midnight: Full Reflexive Chains
hook.content: Link a full French day from morning to night: Le matin, je me lève à sept heures, je me lave et je m'habille. Le soir, je me couche. In the negative, ne steps in BEFORE the reflexive pronoun and pas stands after the verb: Je ne me lève pas tôt!

footnotes.title: How to negate a reflexive verb: ne hugs BOTH the pronoun and the verb
footnotes.content: Because the reflexive pronoun and verb act as one unit, ne...pas wraps the pair together: Je ne me lève pas tôt!

pattern.title: Positive: Je me lève; Negative: Je ne me lève pas; Past: Je me suis levé(e)
pattern.content: Chain daily actions across morning, afternoon, and evening.
pattern.linguist_note: Reflexive clitics form an inseparable phonological unit with the finite verb, so ne precedes the clitic.
pattern.trap_note: Never separate the reflexive pronoun from its verb with ne (*Je me ne lève pas) — write Je ne me lève pas!

exercises.prompt: Match each daily-routine clause with its English meaning:

matching_pairs.english: Je me lève à sept heures
matching_pairs.german: I get up at seven o'clock

matching_pairs.english: Je ne me lève pas tôt le dimanche
matching_pairs.german: I don't get up early on Sundays
I go to bed at midnight

exercises.target_answer: I get up at seven o'clock, I don't get up early on Sundays, I get dressed before coffee, We meet up tonight, I go to bed at midnight
exercises.meaning: Je me lève à sept heures, Je ne me lève pas tôt le dimanche, Je m'habille avant le café, On se retrouve ce soir, Je me couche à minuit
exercises.explanation: ne...pas wraps the entire reflexive pronoun + verb unit.

exercises.prompt: How do you negate 'Je me couche tard' ('I go to bed late')?
options: Je me ne couche pas tard
Je ne couche pas me tard
Je ne me couche pas tard
exercises.target_answer: Je ne me couche pas tard
exercises.meaning: I don't go to bed late
exercises.explanation: ne goes before me couche, and pas goes after it: Je ne me couche pas.

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word structure of 'Je ne me lève pas tôt'?
exercises.german: Je ne me lève pas tôt
options: I not myself raise step early
I myself not get up early
exercises.target_answer: I not myself raise step early
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: I not myself raise step early
exercises.explanation: ne precedes the pronoun-verb unit me lève.

exercises.idea: on Sundays I do not get up early (use Le dimanche, je ne me lève pas tôt)
cues: I do not get up early → je ne me lève pas tôt
idea_parts: negated reflexive → je ne me lève pas tôt
exercises.target_answer: Le dimanche, je ne me lève pas tôt
exercises.meaning: On Sundays, I don't get up early
exercises.explanation: Le dimanche ('on Sundays') + je ne me lève pas tôt.

diagnosis.slip: put ne between me and lève
diagnosis.cue: Place ne before me: je ne me lève pas.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Je me lave, je m'habille et je prends un café
exercises.target_answer: Je me lave, je m'habille et je prends un café
exercises.meaning: I wash up, get dressed, and have a coffee
exercises.affirmation: You chained the morning routine cleanly!

summary.outcome: Chain positive and negative reflexive verbs across a full daily schedule.

use_example.german: La semaine, je me lève tôt, mais le dimanche je me repose.
use_example.english: During the week I get up early, but on Sundays I rest.

summary.takeaway: ne...pas hugs the reflexive pronoun and verb together: Je ne me lève pas.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([5091] Dont & Où): see how De matin à soir leads directly into Dont & Où.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "On Sundays, I don't get up early" in French:
twist.target_answer: Le dimanche, je ne me lève pas tôt
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Le dimanche, je ne me lève pas tôt" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of De matin à soir.

lever.context_phrase: Je me lève à sept heures.
lever.etymology_derivation: Latin levāre 'to lift' — lever, levitate, elevate. se lever: you raise yourself.

laver.english_meaning: to wash (se laver: to wash oneself)
laver.etymology_derivation: Notice French uses the reflexive + definite article for body parts: je me lave les mains.

coucher.english_meaning: to lay down; to put to bed
coucher.etymology_derivation: collocāre 'to place together' → couch — the furniture is the verb, frozen.

depuis.context_translation: I have lived here for three years (lit. I live here since three years).
depuis.etymology_derivation: Because the action is still true right now, French uses the PRESENT tense with depuis!

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.

me.etymology_derivation: Elides to m' before a vowel: il m'écoute.

on.context_translation: Shall we go to the café?
on.etymology_derivation: on is worn-down homme — 'the man says' became 'one says' became spoken French's everyday 'we'. The nasal vowel is the fossil.
